vulnerability.name: CVE-2024-51744
vulnerability.description: Improper error handling in github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v4 ParseWithClaims: a caller inspecting only jwt.ErrTokenExpired can overlook a co-reported jwt.ErrTokenSignatureInvalid.

statements.impact_statement: The advisory affects github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v4 below v4.5.1. No golang-jwt module of any major version is present in FosterStack Cache: it is absent from go.sum, absent from the compiled package set, and absent from the dependency manifest embedded in the released binaries. golang-jwt/jwt/v5 appears in the module requirement graph only as a transitive requirement of packages of prometheus/client_golang and prometheus/common that this project does not import, and v5 is not affected by this advisory in any version range. Independently reproducible: `go version -m fscache` on any released binary lists the complete set of linked dependencies, and `govulncheck ./...` reports no vulnerabilities.
statements.action_statement: No action required. The affected component is not a dependency of this product, so no upgrade applies.
statements.status_notes: Raised by Snyk against the go.mod project as a module-graph finding. Verified against the shipped v0.1.0 binaries on 2026-09-07.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2025-60876
vulnerability.description: BusyBox wget HTTP request-line splitting via crafted request targets.

statements.impact_statement: This statement applies to the :debug image variant of this product across builds. It is scoped by NAME to the cache image in both the published (pkg:oci/cache) and release-candidate (pkg:oci/cache-candidates) repositories, and to busybox 1.37.0 as a subcomponent — deliberately NOT to a single published digest, so a rebuilt or release-candidate :debug image does not re-trip a CVE already adjudicated here (the failure this re-scoping fixes). busybox is present only in the :debug image variant, included solely so an operator can exec an interactive shell (/busybox/sh) for troubleshooting; the production and -fips variants contain no busybox at all. Nothing in this product invokes any busybox applet: the server is a single Go binary that never shells out, so the vulnerable wget code path is never executed during operation. The vulnerability is reachable only by an operator who has already exec'd into the container and runs wget by hand against attacker-supplied input. This statement supersedes the pre-VEX-doctrine suppression that lived in .grype.yaml with the same analysis; the analysis is unchanged, now published in the policy-governed location. Evidence: this answers the grype finding for this CVE against pkg:generic/busybox@1.37.0 in the :debug image (grype's vulnerability DB as of the scan run); trivy and snyk do not report it. Reachability: govulncheck covers the Go module and reports nothing here because busybox is not a Go dependency but a base-image binary the Go server never execs — vulnerable_code_not_in_execute_path. The subcomponent is version-pinned (busybox@1.37.0), so a base-image bump that changes the busybox version re-trips the scanner and forces re-review. Product identity: image scans that expose the image's tags/repo-digest match the image-scoped products (pkg:oci/cache, pkg:oci/cache-candidates); a scan of a locally built image that carries no registry identity (the PR/main from-source candidate loaded into the daemon) exposes no such identifiers, so this statement ALSO lists the vulnerable component itself (pkg:generic/busybox@1.37.0) as a product so the disposition still applies. busybox is only in the :debug variant of this product, so no other image is affected.
statements.action_statement: No action available or required: upstream busybox has no fixed release for this issue as of this statement. The busybox binary ships unmodified from the gcr.io/distroless/static:debug-nonroot base and updates with it; this statement is re-reviewed on every base-image bump.
